items.item_text: Job offer is contingent upon satisfactory clearance based on Background Check results.
May need to work nights, holidays and weekends.
Position is located in Sacramento. (Subject to change based on available funding and program requirements.)

Advanced ability to communicate complex information in a clear and concise manner both verbally and in writing. Skills in scientific graphical representation, scientific writing and experience presenting at scientific conferences (poster, and oral presentations), and delivering forecasts.

Applies extensive knowledge as a research professional with an in-depth understanding of statistical and / or other analysis techniques designed to support research projects of broad scope and complexity. May function as a team lead.

The position manages meteorology scientific and operational studies, and forecast verification projects in collaboration with CW3E Group Leads and FIRO Project Managers. May act as a PI or team lead to guide project execution and resource allocation. The position advises CW3E leadership on strategic expansion opportunities, including external data sharing, forecast enhancement, and product development.

The position applies advanced meteorological expertise and analytical methodologies to lead complex research and operational forecasting projects. Works closely with partner agencies, and often embedded, this role bridges CW3E’s scientific and forecasting advancements, particularly as it relates to atmospheric rivers and weather forecast verification with operational workflows. The position manages projects, possibly serving as PI, multi-agency initiatives, contributes to real-time forecasting and atmospheric reconnaissance, mentors early-career staff, and communicates regularly representing CW3E.

The position leads efforts to translate CW3E research, deterministic/ensemble forecasts, and data products into partner agency operations. Serve as a primary liaison to build strategic alliances and expand the reach of center-developed tools, research and weather forecasts. The position represents CW3E in high-level meetings, media appearances, scientific conferences and will write and contribute to technical reports, and peer-reviewed publications.
The position will support operational flight planning, real-time forecasting, and agency engagement within the AR Recon Program to maximize program benefits and strategic support.
The position will foster a collaborative work environment and actively support/mentor the professional growth of early-career scientists and postdoctoral scholars.

In-depth knowledge of research function. Includes in-depth knowledge of mesoscale and synoptic-scale processes responsible for precipitation variability and extremes, and numerical weather prediction systems and verification techniques.

Advanced skills associated with statistical analysis, database management and systems programming. Includes methods to examine extreme precipitation and forecast models. Knowledge of operational forecasting models and products. Knowledge of observational and reanalysis data sets as applied to meteorology and climate.
Advanced skills in analysis and consultation.
Advanced project management skills. Ability to lead and influence within and external to project team. This includes proposing new analyses, new conceptual ideas, or new workflow recommendations.
Advanced research skills at a level to evaluate alternate solutions and develop recommendations. This includes proposing new analyses, new conceptual ideas, or new workflow recommendations.
Advanced ability to think creatively to recommend action steps or strategize solutions relative to research. This includes proposing strategic solutions.

Excellent interpersonal skills including tact, diplomacy and flexibility with the ability to work independently or within a team framework in conjunction with principles of community with staff, faculty, researchers, and students
